correctness.rationale: Count distinct length-(n+2) outputs of exactly one insertion, without complements. At sites i<j, trimming the common outside portions reduces equality to B_i U=U B_j, where U=w_{i+2}…w_{j+1} and B_i,B_j are the two-letter inserts. For tandem this is exactly period two on w_i…w_{j+1}; equality classes are consecutive runs, giving 1 plus the distance-two inequalities. For two palindromic inserts, if j=i+1 the three aligned letters force the source triple constant. Otherwise the common middle has period two (both copies of U agree at a shift of two); U ends in w_jw_{j+1} whereas the final insert reverses these letters, making the two parity classes equal. Thus nonconstant palindromic sites give distinct outcomes. Constant sites already belong to the tandem set. For a nonconstant palindromic site i and a tandem site j≤i+1, comparison at the two inserted positions excludes equality. If j≥i+2 those positions require w_{i+2}=w_{i+1} and w_{i+3}=w_i; this is sufficient with j=i+2, giving exactly the abba subtraction. Saturation of both positive sums gives the q≥3 extremum and the count. For binary words, the deficit from n is #zeros minus #changes plus #101 in the transition word. A boundary zero-run costs length minus one and an interior run costs length minus two plus the indicator of length one. The all-zero transition word never maximizes. The qualifying runs give the stated generating function and each transition word has two preimages. Uniform expectation uses probability (q-1)/q for either inequality and (q-1)/q³ for each abba correction, with no corrections for n<4.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration is not the unrestricted proof. The recorded 79073-word frozen run is not a fresh independent run.

evidence: Known component formulas do not determine the intersection size. Their transition words 1010001 and 1001001 both have four changes, and in each source two adjacent pairs of palindrome sites merge within constant runs. The first transition word has one 101, whereas the second has none. The frozen proof uses P_i=T_{i+2} as the sufficient witness at an abba and excludes all cross-channel collisions for nonconstant P_i without that pattern.

value.rationale: The distinct descendants are the exact confusability neighborhood for a natural single-error channel permitting either copy orientation. A mixed neighborhood cannot be sized by adding the individual channel formulas. The correction identifies the precise local obstruction, and the alphabet-dependent extremum and binary maximizing census reveal which sources have the largest ambiguity. These exact local counts are useful independently of an optimal global code bound.
residual_risks: This is a neighborhood theorem, not a claim of code capacity or an optimal duplication-correcting code.
